Isolated clusters and lone soldiers are intentional and allowed.
Do not invent arithmetic dependencies. Do not claim soft edges change the authority score of CPI, LFS, etc.

reports.title: Bank for International Settlements (BIS)
reports.notes: Central bankers' bank. Hosts Basel Committee. Regular research and statistics that feed national prudential frameworks (already partially linked via OSFI CAR / Basel in main graph).

reports.title: BIS Annual Economic Report
reports.notes: Distinct from the institutional Annual Report; focuses on economic analysis.

reports.title: World Trade Organization (WTO)
reports.notes: Treaty-based. Trade Policy Review Mechanism and monitoring reports create regular peer-review pressure on members.

reports.title: WTO Trade Monitoring Reports (WTO-wide + G20)
reports.notes: Peer-review transparency exercise. Joint G20 version with OECD/UNCTAD.

reports.title: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
reports.notes: Quota-based membership. Article IV consultations + flagship trilogy create the strongest formal soft-power channel among the set.

reports.title: Article IV Consultation Reports (country)
reports.notes: Direct bilateral soft pressure channel. Canada receives these.

reports.title: Canada: 2025 Article IV Consultation—Press Release and Staff Report
reports.cadence: Country consultation (Board consideration 16 January 2026; published 21 January 2026)
reports.notes: IMF Country Report No. 26/12 (2026/012). Staff report completed 18 December 2025 following discussions ending 4 December 2025. Soft-layer Canada-specific instance. See also Informational Annex for Fund relations (quota data).

reports.title: World Economic Forum (WEF)
reports.notes: Private foundation / multi-stakeholder. Not treaty-based. Influence via agenda-setting, partnership programmes, and Davos ritual. Canadian departments have funded specific WEF projects (documented in order papers).

reports.title: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
reports.notes: Already has hard methodology edges in main graph (SNA, etc.). Soft layer captures Economic Surveys and peer-review processes.

reports.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Canada 2025
reports.notes: DOI https://doi.org/10.1787/28f9e02c-en. Draft discussed by Economic and Development Review Committee 21 January 2025; data cut-off 16 May 2025. Soft-layer Canada-specific instance of the generic country surveys series.

reports.title: G20
reports.notes: Informal but highly consequential. Communiqués and working groups create ritual coordination pressure. Not a formal treaty body.

dependencies.justification: Annual Meeting is the central ritual.
Core ritual of the G20 process.
Senior overlapping participation, shared language on risks/resilience, and reciprocal citation patterns in public remarks. Not a formal dependency. Dates and agendas rarely align tightly.
Same as reverse edge. WEF provides a multi-stakeholder stage; IMF provides the macroeconomic orthodoxy. Mutual awareness is observable but not contractual.

Heavy cross-citation and overlapping central-bank membership. BIS hosts the Basel process that national supervisors (including OSFI) implement; IMF surveillance frequently references BIS statistics and research.
Regular cross-references in flagships and shared work on structural indicators, productivity, and fiscal frameworks. Both produce country surveillance products.
Joint G20 Trade Monitoring reports (WTO + OECD + UNCTAD). Explicit collaborative product.
G20 communiqués routinely task or endorse IMF work (e.g. SDR channeling, debt frameworks). IMF staff papers often respond to G20 priorities. Soft coordination, not hierarchy.
OECD frequently acts as analytical support for G20 workstreams (tax, structural reform, investment). Ritual rather than legal.
G20 trade and investment monitoring mandates feed into WTO/OECD/UNCTAD joint products.
